subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — PoC kickoff prep and artifacts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Victor Chen <victor@acme.ai>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Victor / Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and the technical questions we promised to follow up on so we can scope a PoC: 

Summary of what we heard you need:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target at or below ~250 ms (95th pctl) for your production streaming flows
- Streaming: prefer low-latency streaming responses for multi-turn conversations (SSE or WebSocket acceptable)
- Chunk cadence: ideally 50–200 ms per chunk for responsive UI; want guidance on trade-offs
- Throughput/concurrency: support for ~150–200 req/s and sustained concurrent streams ~100 concurrent users

Questions / next steps for technical alignment:
1) Can you confirm your prioritized TTFT target (median vs 95th vs 99th)? You mentioned 250 ms as a hard target — correct?
2) Do you prefer SSE or WebSocket for the PoC? Any network constraints (proxies, corporate firewalls)?
3) What is your typical request size (tokens in prompt + expected response length)? This helps us size batching/KV cache.
4) Can you share a short window of production traces (anonymized) or representative request QPS?

What we propose from Redwood for the PoC:
- Provide a dedicated test pool with matching model variant and streaming (SSE & WebSocket) enabled.
- Run a 48–72 hour synthetic + replay PoC using your traces to validate TTFT 95th pctl and chunk cadence.
- Share benchmark artifacts and a short SLO proposal doc for your procurement/review.

I've looped in Aditya (solutions) and Neha (customer success) — Aditya will follow up with detailed feasibility and initial benchmark numbers.

Proposed next meeting: Tue Jul 21 at 10:00 AM PT — 30 minutes to agree on trace, protocol, and acceptance criteria. Are you available?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-one-pager.pdf (pdf)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Victor Chen <victor@acme.ai>, Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Victor / Sofia —

Short answers up front then details below:
- Feasibility: Yes — we can meet 95th pctl TTFT <= 250 ms for the model family you described with a dedicated pool + streaming-optimized config. In our internal benchmarks for similar workload shapes we observe median TTFT ~60–90 ms and 95th pctl for first-token ~120–180 ms on a 4xA100-like dedicated pool (workload dependent).
- Throughput/concurrency: the config that hits those TTFT numbers supports sustained 150–250 req/s with ~100 concurrent streaming sessions using continuous batching + prefix KV caching.
- Streaming protocol: both SSE and WebSocket are supported. WebSocket eliminates some HTTP overhead and tends to have slightly lower end-to-end tail latency in flaky networks; SSE can be simpler for browser-only setups.
- Chunk cadence: smaller chunks (50–100 ms cadence) increase perceived responsiveness but slightly raise per-token CPU and network overhead; 150–250 ms cadence reduces overhead but increases perceived latency. For your 220-token responses we recommend targeting ~100–150 ms chunk cadence to balance responsiveness and cost.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short benchmark summary and a cadence chart that shows expected TTFT vs chunk cadence across candidate configs. These are synthetic but representative; we'll run a replay PoC on your traces next.

[Attachment: ttft_benchmark_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: streaming_cadence_chart.png (image)]

Proposed PoC plan (technical):
1) Exchange a short, anonymized trace (10–30 min of representative traffic) and any network constraints.
2) Redwood runs a 48–72 hour replay + synthetic load against a dedicated pool matching your traffic profile.
3) Measure TTFT (median/95/99), chunk cadence distribution, and end-to-end user-perceived latency; iterate on chunk size and batching to meet 95th pctl <=250 ms.
4) Deliver benchmark report and SLO draft for procurement.

I can run the initial benchmark next week if you can share a small trace file. If WebSocket is preferred, we'll enable that for the replay.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
